title: Offline artifact mirror requirements (Private / on-prem + VPC restricted egress)
content:
Context
- Private deployments increasingly run in environments with restricted/no outbound internet (regulated VPCs w/ egress controls, and true air-gapped on-prem).
- Today we assume access to a Redwood-controlled container registry + Helm chart repo + occasional OS package downloads during bootstrap/upgrade. This breaks in: (a) air-gapped; (b) “limited egress with allowlist only”; (c) customers requiring internal artifact provenance scanning before install.

Goal
Define requirements to support customer-provided offline artifact mirrors for:
1) container images (control plane + data plane + dependencies)
2) Helm charts (Redwood charts + subcharts)
3) OS packages / host dependencies (where applicable)

Non-goals (v1)
- Build a full customer-facing “mirror management product.” v1 is configuration + validation + clear workflows.
- Support arbitrary third-party Helm repos/images beyond what Redwood ships (we can allow overrides, but only on a best-effort basis).
- Solve every distro/package manager. We will document a supported matrix and provide hooks for others.

Definitions / environments
- “Offline mirror”: customer-controlled endpoint hosting copies of Redwood artifacts (images/charts/packages) reachable from cluster nodes/install host.
- “Air-gapped”: no network path to Redwood endpoints during install/upgrade.
- “Restricted egress”: egress possible but only to allowlisted internal endpoints; may still allow occasional manual import of artifacts.

Artifact types to mirror
A) Container images
- All images referenced by Redwood Helm charts (control plane + runtime components) including:
  - redwood-control-plane, redwood-console, redwood-router
  - migration job image(s)
  - metrics/logging sidecars if bundled
  - cert-manager / ingress controller if we ship them as part of “batteries included” mode (note: we should prefer “bring your own” here for restricted envs)
- Requirements:
  - Must support overriding image registry host and, optionally, repository prefix.
  - Must support digest pinning (preferred) and tag pinning (allowed but discouraged).
  - Must support private registry auth mechanisms common in enterprises.

B) Helm charts
- Redwood Helm charts + any vendored dependencies.
- Requirements:
  - Must support installing/upgrading with zero external Helm repo access.
  - Must support an internal chart repository OR a filesystem-based chart bundle.
  - Must support chart provenance verification (at minimum: checksums; ideally: Helm provenance or signature).

C) OS packages / host dependencies
- Installer host dependencies may include: kubectl/helm, container runtime tooling, CSI utilities, or platform-specific packages (varies by on-prem packaging mode).
- Requirements:
  - Installer must not attempt live package downloads in air-gapped mode.
  - For restricted egress: must support configuring internal mirrors (e.g., apt/yum) OR provide a documented “pre-stage packages” procedure.
  - Document what is strictly required vs optional (e.g., troubleshooting tools).

Primary user stories
1) On-prem air-gapped customer
- Customer receives a Redwood “upgrade bundle” (or builds their own from published manifests).
- Customer imports artifacts into their internal registry/repo.
- Operator runs installer upgrade pointing at internal endpoints.
- Prechecks validate reachability + artifact completeness before any changes.

2) VPC customer with artifact scanning
- Customer pulls artifacts from Redwood into a quarantine network, scans, then promotes to internal mirror.
- During upgrades, cluster only reaches internal mirror.
- Audit wants evidence that the artifacts installed correspond to a signed Redwood release.

3) Hybrid
- Control plane artifacts mirrored internally; data plane images may be mirrored per-region; chart repo may be internal S3 (private) with short-lived credentials.

Functional requirements (v1)
FR1. Mirror endpoint configuration
- Terraform and installer must accept explicit endpoints for:
  - container registry (e.g., registry.customer.tld/redwood)
  - chart repo (URL) OR local chart path
  - OS package mirrors (optional; may be documented-only in v1 depending on packaging)
- Must allow per-environment config (dev/stage/prod) and per-region overrides.
- Must support custom CA bundle for TLS interception / private PKI.
- Must support HTTP(S) proxy configuration if customer routes internal traffic via proxy.

FR2. Completeness validation (blocking precheck)
- Preflight must validate that all required artifacts for the target version are available from the configured mirrors before proceeding.
- Must produce an actionable diff:
  - missing images (by digest)
  - missing charts (name/version)
  - missing package artifacts (if relevant)
- Precheck should be able to run in “plan-only” mode so customers can stage artifacts ahead of the maintenance window.

FR3. Artifact selection + pinning
- Upgrade plan artifact must include:
  - target release version
  - exact list of images (by digest) and charts (by version)
  - any required migration job images
- Installer should prefer digests over tags to prevent “mutable tag drift.”

FR4. Offline bundle import workflow (documented + optionally scripted)
- Provide a canonical manifest file (machine-readable) listing artifacts required for a release.
- Provide recommended import commands/examples for:
  - OCI registry import (e.g., skopeo/copy) by digest
  - Helm chart upload/push (chartmuseum/OCI)
- If we ship a single “upgrade bundle” for air-gapped, it must contain:
  - manifest
  - checksums/signatures
  - images (as OCI tar) and charts (tgz/oci)
  - optional OS package tarballs when applicable

FR5. Installer behavior in offline mode
- In “offline” mode, any attempt to reach Redwood endpoints must be treated as a configuration error (fail fast), not a long timeout.
- All retry logic must be bounded and provide clear errors (e.g., DNS failure vs 401 vs missing repo).

FR6. Authentication support
- Container registry auth:
  - Basic auth (username/password) OR token
  - Docker config JSON secret support for Kubernetes pulls
  - Support for cloud-specific private registries (ECR/GCR/ACR) is desirable but not required for on-prem; in VPC it’s common.
- Chart repo auth:
  - Basic auth and/or bearer token headers
  - TLS client cert auth (mTLS) desirable; if not supported in v1, must be explicitly documented.

Security requirements
SR1. Integrity verification (minimum)
- Every artifact bundle must include SHA-256 checksums for:
  - chart files
  - image tarballs (if distributed as files)
  - manifest(s)
- Installer must verify checksums before applying.

SR2. Authenticity / signing (target)
- Prefer a signing mechanism that works offline:
  - Option A: GPG-signed manifest + published public key (offline verifiable)
  - Option B: Cosign signatures attached to OCI artifacts (works offline if signatures are mirrored too)
- Requirement: installer must verify signature for the target release in “strict” mode, and must be able to run in “warn-only” mode for early adoption.
- Document key rotation policy + how customers obtain/validate Redwood public keys.

SR3. Least privilege + secrets handling
- Mirror credentials must be provided via:
  - Kubernetes secrets for pull creds
  - installer config file with optional env var injection
  - never printed in logs; redact in plan output and support bundles
- Support KMS/HSM-managed secrets where applicable (especially VPC).

SR4. Auditability
- Upgrade plan should record mirror endpoints used (sanitized) and artifact digests.
- Emit audit log events (control plane) noting:
  - “upgrade started” with target version
  - “artifact verification passed/failed” with counts (not raw creds)
  - “bundle signature verified” (true/false; strict/warn)

SR5. Vulnerability scanning compatibility
- Provide an inventory file (SBOM or at least a list of images+digest) per release.
- Customers should be able to run scanners against mirrored artifacts without requiring Redwood services.

Reliability requirements
RR1. Deterministic installs/upgrades
- Given the same manifest + mirrored artifacts, two installs must fetch identical digests.
- No background “latest” resolution.

RR2. Performance / time bounds
- Precheck should complete within 5 minutes for a typical deployment when mirrors are reachable.
- Provide ability to parallelize artifact head checks.

RR3. Failure modes
- Missing artifact: hard fail before any Helm upgrade/migration job execution.
- Auth failure: fail with exact endpoint + recommended remediation (e.g., test curl/helm registry login).
- TLS failure: include hint about custom CA bundle.

Compatibility / constraints
- Air-gapped customers often have:
  - internal DNS naming conventions; no public DNS resolution
  - TLS interception or private CA
  - strict egress firewall requiring explicit allowlists
  - registry policy requiring namespace whitelisting
- On-prem clusters may not support:
  - OCI registry for Helm charts (still common to use ChartMuseum)
  - S3-backed chart repos

Proposed configuration surface (strawman)
Installer config keys (names TBD):
- artifacts.mode = online | restricted | offline
- artifacts.registry.endpoint = registry.customer.tld
- artifacts.registry.repository_prefix = redwood
- artifacts.registry.auth = secretRef/dockerconfigjson OR user/pass
- artifacts.charts.mode = repo | oci | local
- artifacts.charts.endpoint = https://charts.customer.tld/redwood
- artifacts.charts.local_path = /mnt/redwood/charts
- artifacts.tls.ca_bundle_path = /etc/ssl/customer-ca.pem
- artifacts.verification.checksums = required
- artifacts.verification.signature = strict | warn | disabled

Terraform variables (draft)
- private_artifact_registry_endpoint
- private_artifact_chart_repo_endpoint
- private_artifact_offline_mirror_endpoints (list form for multi-region)
- private_upgrade_window (ties into release train + maintenance planning)

Open questions / TODO
- Do we standardize on cosign for images AND charts (OCI) or use GPG-signed manifest for everything? (Leaning: GPG-signed manifest for v1 due to offline simplicity; add cosign later.)
- For Helm: do we officially support both ChartMuseum and OCI registries in v1? What’s our minimum Kubernetes/Helm version requirement?
- Do we need first-class support for “multiple registries” (control plane images in one, data plane in another)? This is common for customers with separate security zones.
- OS packages: what exactly does the installer pull today in the on-prem path vs what is included in the on-prem bundle? Need a definitive list and ownership.

Acceptance criteria (v1)
- A fully air-gapped upgrade succeeds using only customer mirrors + bundle artifacts.
- Precheck blocks upgrade when any artifact is missing and prints a concise missing list.
- Operator can generate a manifest for target version (plan-only) without applying changes.
- Signature/checksum verification is implemented and exercised in CI (at least one offline scenario).
- Docs include a step-by-step “import to mirror” guide and troubleshooting for the top 5 errors (401, x509, missing digest, chart not found, DNS).

Notes from infra/security review (snippets)
- Security asked that verification happens before writing anything to the cluster (no partial state changes) and that we never log credentials.
- For enterprise audit, recording digests is more valuable than tags; tags are allowed but must be clearly marked as mutable.

Next steps
- Align with Release Eng on the canonical manifest format + where it’s published per release (ties to Private release train).
- Align with Installer team on precheck UI/UX and strict vs warn modes.
- Produce a small design doc addendum for signing choice and key distribution.
- Add one e2e CI lane for offline mirror scenario (can be local registry + local chart repo in CI) and gate private releases on it (phased rollout).
